## What The Business Is

Coherent Corp. is a global photonics and compound-semiconductor company serving communications, AI data centers, industrial lasers, instrumentation, electronics, and materials markets. The company describes itself as a “global photonics leader” with core capabilities in materials, optics, lasers, thermoelectrics, and networking products. ([coherent.com](https://www.coherent.com/company/about-us?utm_source=openai))

## What It Does

Coherent makes optical components, transceivers, lasers, engineered materials, thermoelectric products, and photonic subsystems used to move, generate, shape, and manage light. Its current growth center is Datacenter & Communications: 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers, ZR/ZR+ coherent modules, optical circuit switches, indium phosphide photonic devices, and co-packaged optics for AI data-center networks. It also sells industrial laser and materials products used in semiconductor equipment, manufacturing, medical, and scientific applications. ([coherent.com](https://www.coherent.com/?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Coherent’s May 6, 2026 fiscal Q3 report showed record quarterly revenue of **$1.81 billion**, up **21% year over year**, with non-GAAP gross margin of **39.6%** and non-GAAP EPS of **$1.41**; management guided fiscal Q4 revenue to **$1.91 billion–$2.05 billion**. ([coherent.com](https://www.coherent.com/content/dam/coherent/site/en/documents/investors/financial-releases/2026/may-6/earnings-release-fy26-q3.pdf?utm_source=openai)) In the call excerpt, management said Datacenter & Communications represented **75%** of revenue, data-center revenue rose **37% year over year**, communications rose **60%**, backlog reached a record level, and orders extended into calendar 2028.

Capacity expansion is central to the bull case: management said 6-inch indium phosphide yields are exceeding legacy 3-inch lines and that internal InP capacity should double by calendar 2026, one quarter earlier than originally planned, then more than double again by the end of calendar 2027. On June 16, 2026, the U.S. Commerce Department announced a letter of intent for up to **$50 million** in CHIPS funding to expand Coherent’s Sherman, Texas 6-inch InP facility; Coherent said the project would double manufacturing space and quadruple wafer capacity. ([nist.gov](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/06/department-commerces-chips-program-announces-letter-intent-coherent-50?utm_source=openai))

NVIDIA’s recently announced strategic partnership remains a major validation signal. NVIDIA and Coherent announced a partnership to develop optics technology for next-generation data-center architecture, and the transcript notes a **$2 billion NVIDIA equity investment** plus a multiyear supply agreement extending through the end of the decade, covering CPO-related products including high-power continuous-wave lasers. ([nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-coherent-announce-strategic-partnership-to-develop-optics-technology-to-scale-next-generation-data-center-architecture?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

Execution risk is high because the growth plan depends on rapid capacity ramps in constrained technologies. Management explicitly identified indium phosphide as an industry-wide bottleneck, and Reuters reported in June 2026 that China’s export restrictions on InP threaten AI data-center rollouts; the report said average 6-inch InP wafer prices had risen **250% to $5,000** since restrictions began. ([m.investing.com](https://m.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/chinas-control-over-indium-phosphide-exports-threatens-ai-data-centre-rollout-4736446?ampMode=1&utm_source=openai))

Capital intensity is rising. In fiscal Q3, Coherent’s capex increased to **$290 million** from **$154 million** in the prior quarter and **$112 million** a year earlier, and management said capex would increase sequentially again in fiscal Q4 to support data-center and communications demand. ([coherent.com](https://www.coherent.com/content/dam/coherent/site/en/documents/investors/financial-releases/2026/may-6/earnings-release-fy26-q3.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The business mix is increasingly tied to AI optical-networking adoption timelines. The transcript frames CPO, OCS, multi-rail, and thermal solutions as future growth vectors, but several are still ramping or expected to begin revenue contribution later, including multi-rail in first-half calendar 2027 and thermal products in second-half calendar 2027. Industrial also remains soft: management said Industrial revenue declined modestly sequentially and year over year, reflecting weakness in parts of the broader industrial market.

## Bull Case
Revenue is accelerating at 21% YoY with Q4 guidance of $1.91–2.05B, putting the forward revenue run-rate near $8.5B+. Datacenter & Communications at 75% of revenue and growing 37–60% YoY, backed by a record backlog extending into calendar 2028, provides strong revenue visibility. The NVIDIA strategic partnership ($2B equity investment, multiyear supply agreement through end of decade) validates Coherent's CPO and optical technology positioning. CHIPS funding of $50M for the Sherman InP facility and accelerated 6-inch InP capacity ramp (doubling by end of 2026, then doubling again by end of 2027) could alleviate the InP bottleneck and restore FCF as capex normalizes. If capex peaks in fiscal Q4 and begins tapering in calendar 2027, forward FCF could recover toward $300–400M from the current -$538M trough, with a path to $700M+ normalized FCF on ~$9B revenue at 40% gross margins.

## Bear Case
TTM FCF is deeply negative at -$538M and capex is still rising sequentially ($112M → $154M → $290M per quarter), with management guiding another increase in fiscal Q4. China's InP export restrictions have driven 6-inch wafer prices up 250% to $5,000, threatening margins and capacity ramps. Several growth vectors (multi-rail, thermal products) won't contribute revenue until H1/H2 calendar 2027, meaning the 12-month forward window captures mostly the high-capex, low-FCF phase. Industrial remains soft. Current EV of $63B against negative FCF implies the market is pricing in near-perfect execution on capacity, demand, and supply constraints—a precarious setup if any ramp slips.

## Logic
**Forward FCF estimate:** TTM FCF is -$538M due to capex surging to ~$290M/quarter (~$1.16B annualized). Over the next 12 months, revenue should reach ~$8.5B (Q4 guide midpoint ~$1.98B quarterly, growing). At ~40% gross margin, gross profit approaches $3.4B. Operating cash flow could reach ~$1.1–1.3B. Assuming capex remains elevated but begins moderating in the back half as InP capacity comes online, I estimate full-year forward capex of ~$950M, yielding forward FCF of approximately **$250M**—a meaningful recovery from the trough but still well below the $256M generated two years ago on lower revenue.

**Applied EV/FCF multiple:** Forward FCF is at a cyclical trough, so applying a static multiple understates the business. The market is effectively pricing normalized FCF (~$700M) at ~85–90x. I apply **120x** on the depressed $250M forward FCF, which implies ~$42–43x on a normalized $700M FCF—reasonable for an AI-infrastructure growth company with NVIDIA validation but tempered by InP supply risk and execution uncertainty. This yields a forward EV of $30,000M.

**EV-to-market-cap bridge:** Current EV minus market cap gap = $63,246.6M – $61,456.2M = **$1,790.4M** (net cash/debt equivalent). Applying this gap: forward market cap = $30,000M – $1,790.4M = **$28,209.6M**.
